audit_narrative: Illustrative example only. ISSUE-000 was reported as a Critical NoSQL injection ([issue](../../../.github/docs/00-issues/issue-register.xlsx)). The root cause analyst traced it to string-concatenated BasicQuery construction ([root cause](../../../.github/docs/02-root-cause/root_cause_ISSUE-000.md)); the blast radius analyst scoped it to one endpoint with no wider service impact ([blast radius](../../../.github/docs/03-blast-radius/blast_radius_ISSUE-000.md)). The fix strategist proposed a Criteria-based parameterised query citing CWE-943 ([fix plan](../../../.github/docs/04-fix-plans/fix_plan_ISSUE-000.md)), approved by a human. The fixer drafted and compiled the patch ([fix](../../../.github/docs/05-fixes/fix_ISSUE-000.md)). All three Step 1 checks passed ([re-scan](../../../.github/docs/06-verify/rescan_ISSUE-000.md), [red-team](../../../.github/docs/06-verify/redteam_ISSUE-000.md), [behavior](../../../.github/docs/06-verify/behavior_ISSUE-000.md)), the QA gate passed with a new mocked regression test ([qa](../../../.github/docs/09-qa/qa_ISSUE-000.md)), and the build gate passed with no dependency drift ([build](../../../.github/docs/10-build/build_ISSUE-000.md)). The merge arbiter scored it 100/100 against a 90-point threshold and cleared it ([verdict](../../../.github/docs/11-ship/verdict_ISSUE-000.md)).
pr_summary: Replaces string-concatenated BasicQuery construction in EmployeeSearchRepository with a parameterised Criteria/Query, closing a NoSQL injection in the employee search endpoint.
No API, return type, or call-site changes — behavior for legitimate searches is unchanged.
pr_test_plan: New mocked regression test (EmployeeSearchRepositoryTest) verifying the constructed Criteria binds the reported injection payload as a literal value — passed.
mvn verify for employee-service — passed, no dependency drift.
Not run in CI (no live MongoDB in this environment): the original @DataMongoTest suite — run manually against a real MongoDB before merging if that suite isn't exercised elsewhere in CI.
